Herbie Flowers.question: In 1998 session drummer _____ again teamed up with Flowers to form a rhythm section in musical settings of the words of poet Sir John Betjeman on a second album they recorded together
Herbie Flowers.fact: In 1998 session drummer Peter Boita again teamed up with Flowers to form a rhythm section in musical settings of the words of poet Sir John Betjeman on a second album they recorded together.

Herbie Flowers.subject: Applied Sciences
Herbie Flowers.question: Boita and Flowers reprised their roles when Poetry in Motion was performed live for a charity show at the _____ on 5 April 1992
Herbie Flowers.fact: Boita and Flowers reprised their roles when Poetry in Motion was performed live for a charity show at the Richmond Theatre on 5 April 1992.

Herbie Flowers.subject: Applied Sciences
Herbie Flowers.question: He created his most famous bassline for _____'s 1972 hit single "Walk on the Wild Side" from the album Transformer
Herbie Flowers.fact: Flowers contributed to recordings by Elton John, Camel, David Bowie, Lou Reed, Roy Harper, David Essex, Al Kooper, Bryan Ferry, Harry Nilsson, Cat Stevens, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr. He created his most famous bassline for Lou Reed's 1972 hit single "Walk on the Wild Side" from the album Transformer.

Herbie Flowers.question: After hearing an electric bass at a New York nightclub, he acquired his own solid-body electric instrument, a _____ 1960 Fender Jazz Bass that he purchased from Manny's Music in New York City for $79
Herbie Flowers.fact: After hearing an electric bass at a New York nightclub, he acquired his own solid-body electric instrument, a Lake Placid Blue 1960 Fender Jazz Bass that he purchased from Manny's Music in New York City for $79.
